# V1 implementation and stacked-PR execution

Status: active execution portfolio. Baseline: `origin/main` at `07154021c` (0.10.2). [Task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

The current-contract repairs (release-PR compatibility, installer fidelity, schemas, durable versions, native dependencies, lockfiles, interrupted versioning, binary inventory and native authentication) shipped in 0.10.0 to 0.10.2. What remains is the D01-gated model work, the effect and registry-completion stacks, intent-selected workflow outputs and the production verification pass. Architectural D01 choices, remote delivery and publication remain separate decisions.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects | T08 shared physical effects | One owner per irreversible effect; the tag and announcement already wait for every registry publish and a local rerun completes a failed release, so what remains is executing a shared effect once |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, canonical-only new exact references, registry publication before shared tags/public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. Remaining wire shapes and migration rules below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | The owner chose canonical slash-qualified IDs for every new exact reference; reject new bare and colon-form aliases, and read existing forms only through an explicit ownership migration boundary | Specify which historical records remain readable and how migration is surfaced; cover config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy bare key may resolve to an owner that already has a canonical key in the same file | Choose behavior when both keys carry different versions; current `or_insert` keeps the canonical value and silently drops the migrated legacy value |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | The owner chose required Cargo/npm/PyPI publications before a shared tag and public GitHub release; a future Go source tag can itself be a publication | Specify draft creation and upload ordering and prove all required owner outputs complete before public announcement |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Package owners control hook scripts and any effects they initiate; Callisto preserves native behavior and does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks | Settled owner boundary: preserve it in future publisher changes; do not require hook migration or promise that external hook effects are coordinated |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics

Use Git worktrees and native GitHub stacks.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from a dirty shared checkout.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); plain chained PRs targeting a parent branch get no CI because `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` triggers only for PRs targeting `main`. Each PR must pass `just ci` on its own.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

## Plugin execution route

Use a light route for existing defects and the fuller route only when a domain contract changes. Do not make every small shell patch run the complete requirement lifecycle.

| Situation | Plugins/skills | Artifact or check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already verified current-contract defect | Navigator packet → Smith bounded implementation → Ranger targeted sibling/defect-family review → Sentinel scoped verification | Exact diff, regression/fault evidence, current criterion mapping and remaining checks |
| Canonical ownership, native authority or output-proof change | Scribe architecture/spec work and applicable audit/verify/gate steps → Navigator amendment → Smith → independent review/Sentinel | Owner-confirmed contract, versioned wire policy, interface inventory and raw spec hash |
| New domain gap discovered during implementation | Stop only that batch; Scribe architect/spec correction and Navigator amendment | Evidence-backed escalation; do not silently invent a second semantic model |
| New request beyond this scope | Weaver capture/connect/clarify only as needed | Traceable need; no unapproved requirement becomes a gate |
| User-visible release impact | Courier changeset | Verified topic-specific entry targeting `callisto-cli` |
| Commit and stacked PR handoff | Courier commit/PR after permission | Parent-only diff, full-stack evidence, base branch, migration risks and authorized remote action |

Plugins guide reasoning and evidence; they do not themselves provide isolated worktrees, a branch scheduler or authorization. Final synthesis, interface decisions and binding readiness stay with the coordinator. Sentinel must report pending/unverifiable evidence rather than converting a targeted test into a whole-release pass.

## Agent and model allocation

Prefer the host's inherited model unless a bounded job benefits from a deliberate smaller override. The currently exposed delegation runtime permits `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and the parent frontier model; do not rely on unavailable role-card model names or promise costs/latencies.

| Work | Allocation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paths, symbols, test commands and branch/CI inventory | `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, recon | Read-only deterministic inventory; no architectural verdict |
| Shell installer fixtures, link/schema checks, fixed doc edits | Small model at low/medium effort where the interface is fixed | Explicit files and expected cases; escalate failed reasoning instead of lowering verification |
| Straightforward parser/lock/auth correction | Workhorse model, medium effort; raise effort for alias/auth subtleties | One subsystem, fixed owner contract and native regression |
| Canonical identity, historical authority, DAG/proofs and partial-upload semantics | Coordinator/strong model, high effort | Own cross-crate interfaces and failure semantics; no concurrent competing models |
| Implementation once interfaces are fixed | Workhorse implementer, medium/high effort | One isolated task/worktree with no shared write set |
| Independent challenge/review | Separate workhorse reviewer, high effort for model/retry changes | Read final diff plus tests; never rely on the author's self-certification |

Start with two implementing workers plus one read-only reviewer/recon, not an agent per finding. Increase concurrency only when there are disjoint, unblocked tasks and the coordinator can inspect every result. A packet contains objective, persisted paths/hashes, owned files, exclusions, criterion/test cases, dependencies and a completion condition. Workers preserve other changes and return changed paths, commands, actual outcomes, skips and unresolved concerns.

For parallel lanes, shared specs, architecture/README/operator docs, changeset creation and the repository Cargo.lock are coordinator-owned integration surfaces. Workers return proposed amendments for those files rather than editing them concurrently; the coordinator applies them on each PR branch before its final checks. Reserve shared Rust source and integration-test files explicitly before delegation; serialize packets whose write sets overlap. A forked agent conversation is not filesystem isolation: verify its actual worktree before allowing writes.

No concurrent Cargo builds/tests locally, even across tasks. Reserve one build slot; use sequential scoped runs and reuse the shared cache. Read-only analysis, shell-only tests, review and drafting can run while that slot is occupied. Worktree/build-directory changes need approval where they change environment or resource use; they are not a reason to bypass the repository's build rule.

## Interface sibling inventory

| Shared contract | Confirmed participants | Required disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Manifest` / `ManifestIdentity` / `VersionSource` | `CargoToml`, `PackageJson`, `PyprojectToml`; `read_identity`; live base-version and historical blob readers | T06-HISTORY and T07 migrate all reached readers/editors, including writers and snapshots; preserve native parsing and format rules |
| Selector ownership | `IdentityIndex`; add/status/aggregate/matrix; config rules/groups; `history.rs::sole_owner_at` and pre-state/history readers | T06/T06-HISTORY unify exact selectors, distinguish glob syntax and migrate both tag/pre-state ownership consumers |
| `ReleaseProviderSet` | Production `ValidatedReleaseIntent` and simulator `SimWorld` | T08 migrates both; fake CLI provider harness still exercises real dispatch |
| Registry adapter/evidence | `CargoRegistry`, `NpmRegistry`, `PypiRegistry`; platform npm path | T08 gives every reached sibling a migrated or evidence-backed unaffected disposition |
| Immutable release wires | Decision, input snapshot, intent, artifact manifest, envelope, receipt, schemas; CLI file/stdout producers and action scripts | D01 fixes compatibility; T08 migrates producers/consumers, including CLI registry-only inventory acceptance/envelope sealing and local build preparation |
| Selected builds and auth | Generated simple/matrix workflows, shared action execution, build matrix/placement, policy/contract tests | T12 verifies all routes, not just this repo's custom workflow; lifecycle scripts remain package-owner-controlled |

This is an inspected candidate inventory, not a promise that no new call site exists. Each implementer re-runs syntactic and responsibility-based searches on its actual base. An external lifecycle hook or unavailable native environment remains an explicit coverage gap.

## Verification at each boundary

1. Record baseline and test prerequisites; write a failing reachable regression before the correction where feasible. Check the exact parent delta and structurally identical siblings.
2. Run the scoped commands in the task JSON sequentially; use native pack/install/build evidence where semantics require it. Test negative, stale, partial and conflicting states, not only a successful fresh release.

Status: active execution portfolio. Baseline: `origin/main` at `07154021c` (0.10.2). [Task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

The current-contract repairs (release-PR compatibility, installer fidelity, schemas, durable versions, native dependencies, lockfiles, interrupted versioning, binary inventory and native authentication) shipped in 0.10.0 to 0.10.2. What remains is the D01-gated model work, the effect and registry-completion stacks, intent-selected workflow outputs and the production verification pass. Architectural D01 choices, remote delivery and publication remain separate decisions.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects | T08 shared physical effects | One owner per irreversible effect; the tag and announcement already wait for every registry publish and a local rerun completes a failed release, so what remains is executing a shared effect once |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, canonical-only new exact references, registry publication before shared tags/public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. Remaining wire shapes and migration rules below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | The owner chose canonical slash-qualified IDs for every new exact reference; reject new bare and colon-form aliases, and read existing forms only through an explicit ownership migration boundary | Specify which historical records remain readable and how migration is surfaced; cover config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy bare key may resolve to an owner that already has a canonical key in the same file | Choose behavior when both keys carry different versions; current `or_insert` keeps the canonical value and silently drops the migrated legacy value |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | The owner chose required Cargo/npm/PyPI publications before a shared tag and public GitHub release; a future Go source tag can itself be a publication | Specify draft creation and upload ordering and prove all required owner outputs complete before public announcement |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Package owners control hook scripts and any effects they initiate; Callisto preserves native behavior and does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks | Settled owner boundary: preserve it in future publisher changes; do not require hook migration or promise that external hook effects are coordinated |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics

Use Git worktrees and native GitHub stacks.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from a dirty shared checkout.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); plain chained PRs targeting a parent branch get no CI because `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` triggers only for PRs targeting `main`. Each PR must pass `just ci` on its own.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.

# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Proposed decision

- Use canonical slash-qualified distribution references for new exact inputs, authored and generated data; reject new bare and colon-form aliases. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Read existing bare/colon references only through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary with established ownership. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.

## Canonical references and migration

- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

## Prior art and research limits

| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |

Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).

Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Non-goals

No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

| Surface | Accepts | Emits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release wire (decision, intent, snapshot, manifest, receipt) | `ecosystem/native-name` only | same |

| `product-package`, `[[release.artifact]] package` | qualified only; bare gives E197 | n/a |

| | Readers | Writers | Cost | Cost to users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Exit code 1
# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.

## Canonical references and migration

- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.

callisto 0.11.0
Changesets-style version and release manager for Rust workspaces

Usage: callisto [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add          Create a new changeset describing pending package changes
  status       Show the workspace's pending changesets and diagnostics
  version      Consume pending changesets and bump package versions accordingly
  pre          Manage prerelease mode for the workspace
  snapshot     Apply a temporary, non-persistent version bump for a snapshot release
  init         Scaffold Callisto configuration in the current workspace
  release      Publish every package whose current version has not been released yet
  completions  Generate shell completion scripts

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>  Output format for command results [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --cwd <CWD>        Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory) [default: .]
      --dry-run          Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
Scaffold Callisto configuration in the current workspace

Usage: callisto init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>                Output format for command results [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --yes                            Run without prompts; required when stdin is not a terminal
      --cwd <CWD>                      Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory) [default: .]
      --versioning <VERSIONING>        Whether packages share one version (fixed) or version independently [possible values: fixed, independent]
      --artifact-target <TRIPLE>       Ship the product's binaries as GitHub release assets for this Rust target triple (repeatable, comma-separated)
      --dry-run                        Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk
      --product-package <PACKAGE>      The package whose binaries ship, when several packages produce one
      --forge-repository <OWNER/REPO>  The GitHub repository (`owner/repo`) binaries are released to
      --workflow                       Generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`
      --no-workflow                    Do not generate a GitHub Actions release workflow
  -h, --help                           Print help
Create a new changeset describing pending package changes

Usage: callisto add [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>          Output format for command results [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --package <NAME:SEVERITY>  Package and severity to include, as `name:severity` (none, patch, minor, or major); repeatable. Omit to enter the interactive wizard
      --cwd <CWD>                Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory) [default: .]
      --summary <SUMMARY>        Human-readable summary of the change to record in the changeset
      --dry-run                  Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk
  -h, --help                     Print help
Publish every package whose current version has not been released yet

Usage: callisto release [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>           Output format for command results [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --cwd <CWD>                 Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory) [default: .]
      --dry-run                   Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk
      --package <ECOSYSTEM/NAME>  Release only this exact qualified package, for example `cargo/callisto-cli`. Repeatable
      --receipt <FILE>            Also write the release receipt to this file
  -h, --help                      Print help

content.content:
Dependency-aware, changeset-driven versioning and releases for Cargo, npm, and PyPI monorepos.

--- Callisto turns per-package changesets into a version plan for Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI workspaces. It reads native manifests to decide which dependents need updates, then prepares the files and release operations for review. ## A change through Callisto Suppose `service` depends on a Cargo crate `core` at `^0.2`. A contributor records a minor change to `core`: ```sh callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API" callisto version --dry-run ``` With the default cascade policy, the plan is: | Package | Before | Planned change | | --- | --- | --- | | `core` | `0.2.0` | `0.3.0` from the changeset | | `service` | `1.4.2`, requires `core ^0.2` | `1.4.3` from the default patch cascade; requirement updated to `^0.3` | | Unrelated npm or Python package | Its current version | No bump just because it shares the repo | The dependency requirement triggers the `service` bump; sharing a repo does not. Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Explicit version groups can couple packages that should move together. - `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs for review and commit. - The release workflow uses native publishers and coordinates configured tags, GitHub releases, and assets. Package owners retain their hooks and credentials. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; changesets["Changesets
release intent"] --> plan["Version plan
dependency-aware"] manifests[("Native manifests
Cargo · npm/pnpm · Python")] --> plan plan --> updates["Version updates
manifests · changelogs · lockfiles"] updates --> review{{"Review and commit
versioned state"}} review --> release["Release
configured operations"] release --> outputs(["Packages · tags · GitHub releases"]) class changesets source class manifests store class plan,updates,release engine class review router class outputs output ``` Callisto is pre-v1. The [guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md) covers current support, known limits, and when another tool may be a better fit. ## Install **proto** ([moonrepo/proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto)), from a release binary: ```toml # .prototools [plugins.tools] callisto = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orin-dx/callisto/main/proto/callisto.toml" ``` ```bash proto install callisto ``` **cargo**, built from source (package `callisto-cli`, binary `callisto`): ```bash cargo install callisto-cli ``` **Release binaries**, from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases) (tag `callisto@`): ```bash curl -sL "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/callisto@/callisto-.tar.gz" | tar -xz ``` Available targets: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. ## Quick start Start in a Git repository with an `origin` push URL and crates.io credentials. This registry-only example publishes a crate and creates a tag; it does not build assets or create a GitHub Release. See [releasing](docs/releasing.md) for CI and product releases. ```bash # 1. Scaffold callisto.toml and .changeset/ in the workspace root callisto init --yes --versioning independent --no-workflow # 2. Record a pending change against a package callisto add --package cargo/my-crate:minor --summary "Add authentication middleware" # 3. See pending changesets and the version bumps they imply callisto status # 4. Commit the configuration and pending change git add callisto.toml .changeset/ git commit -m "chore: configure releases and record pending changes" # 5. Consume changesets, bump manifests, update changelogs and lockfiles callisto version # 6. Commit the staged release changes; release requires a clean checkout git commit -m "chore(release): version packages" # 7. Preview, then publish callisto release --dry-run callisto release ``` Run `callisto --help` for prerelease mode, snapshots, CI checks, JSON output, and shell completions. ## Documentation - [Guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md): release model, example, and supported layouts. - [Releasing](docs/releasing.md): local and CI workflows, limits, and recovery. - [Publishing](docs/publishing.md): registry credentials. - [Configuration](docs/config.md) and [errors](docs/errors.md): references. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security](SECURITY.md): project information. ## License Mixed: `callisto-model` is MIT; the rest of the workspace is [FSL-1.1-MIT](LICENSE) (becomes MIT two years after each version's release). adr/ architecture/ projects/ specs/ config.md 8.6K errors.md 41.6K how-callisto-works.md 5.2K publishing.md 6.4K releasing.md 8.9K

# Publishing: registry authentication

Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).

Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

### Provenance

Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.

---

## Cargo (crates.io)

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.

---

## Python (PyPI)

Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.

Map the generated workflow's `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_PASSWORD` in the publishing job. The secret name alone does not configure Twine.

### Generated Callisto workflows

Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.

# How Callisto works

Callisto turns changesets and native package metadata into a version plan. It then coordinates the selected registry, Git, and GitHub operations. Current scope is Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI.

## Where it fits

Use Callisto when contributors should declare release impact and a repo needs native dependency updates across its supported package types. The version plan makes each bump reviewable before publication.

Other tools may fit your existing workflow:

- [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) focuses on npm package releases.
- [Knope](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) offers configurable release workflows.
- [Nx Release](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases) integrates with Nx projects and tasks.
- [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/design.md) builds release PRs from conventional commits.

## A change through the system

Suppose a Cargo crate `service` depends on `core`. A contributor records a change to `core`:

```sh
callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API"
callisto status
callisto version --dry-run
```

Callisto builds the version plan from the changeset, manifests, and `callisto.toml`:

- The changeset requests a minor bump for `core`.
- The Cargo dependency in `service` tells Callisto whether the new version fits its existing requirement.
  - Under the default `out-of-range` policy, a version outside that requirement can bump `service` and update its dependency declaration.
  - Cascade mode and bump severity are configurable.
- Fixed and linked groups can add packages through explicit policy.
- Unrelated npm and Python packages do not join solely because they share the repo.

After reviewing the plan, `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs. It stages the versioned state for a commit. `callisto release --dry-run` then previews the release operations.

## The model

| Concept | What it means today |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace package | A dependency graph node located from source and manifests. |
| Distribution | A native Cargo, npm, or PyPI identity described by a manifest. One package can expose multiple supported distributions. |
| Native dependency | A manifest relationship that can affect dependent versions and publication order. |
| Version group | An explicit fixed or linked rule in `callisto.toml`. |
| Release operation | One registry, tag, GitHub release, or asset effect with prerequisites. |

These relationships serve different purposes. For example, a Rust library embedded in a Python wheel is a build input. That alone does not create a Cargo registry dependency or make the crate and wheel share a version. See [configuration](config.md) for supported dependency and version-group rules.

## Releasing and recovery

- **Local release:** `callisto release --dry-run` previews the plan. `callisto release` runs it from a clean checkout.
  - Native publishers use their own credentials.
- **Managed CI:** The version PR commits the selected package and version decision. CI verifies it after merge.
  - Planning declares operations. Building creates artifacts. Execution receives registry credentials.
- **Execution:** Callisto checks each provider before acting.
  - It adopts an exact match, performs and confirms an absent effect, and stops on a conflict or indeterminate result.
  - A receipt records the evidence collected.

Release operations follow known dependency and platform prerequisites. They do not follow a fixed Cargo, npm, then PyPI sequence. The [release guide](releasing.md) covers the local and CI paths, retries, and recovery.

## Current support

Callisto is pre-v1. These rows describe current behavior rather than planned adapters.

| Ecosystem | Versioning | Publishing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cargo | Crate versions, supported dependency declarations, lockfiles | Cargo |
| npm/pnpm | Package versions, supported native dependency forms, lockfiles | Native npm tooling |
| Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |

| Layout | Current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
| napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets. Its workspace wide roster can include unrelated addons. |
| Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
| Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |

Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:

- A multi-registry release is not atomic.

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` can print `Nothing to release.` without a receipt.

- That message is not proof of completion.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build/placement roster is currently workspace-wide, not narrowed to the release intent. Unrelated addons can block a release; this is tracked for correction, not a support requirement.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

# Security Policy

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Email **security@orin-dx.com** — don't open a public issue for anything that could be exploited before a fix ships.

Include:
- Which crate or code path is affected
- The concrete failure scenario — what an attacker could do, and how
- Steps to reproduce, if you have them

Expect an acknowledgment within 5 business days. We'll keep you posted as a fix moves through triage, and credit you in the release notes unless you'd rather stay anonymous.

## Scope

Callisto edits manifests and pushes releases across multiple package registries from inside CI, so the threat model is higher-stakes than a typical CLI tool:

- **Registry token exposure** — Callisto's own release workflow (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) grants `contents`/`pull-requests` write only to the jobs that need them (`version-pr`, `execute`); registry credentials (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, and `NPM_TOKEN`/`TWINE_PASSWORD` for workspaces that publish npm/PyPI packages) reach only the `execute` job. A way to make Callisto, or the in-repo `.github/actions/callisto-action`, exfiltrate those tokens, or publish to a package other than the one it was asked to, is a critical finding.
- **Workflow/action injection** — Callisto is designed to run unattended on `push` to `main` in downstream repos. An untrusted PR that could get its content executed by the release workflow (rather than merely analyzed) is in scope.
- **Manifest parser safety** — `callisto-manifests` edits `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` via CST-preserving parsers (`toml_edit`, `serde_json`) rather than regex specifically to avoid corruption; a crafted manifest that causes incorrect writes, path traversal, or a crash mid-write (bypassing the atomic `NamedTempFile` + `fs::rename` guarantee) is a real finding.
- **Version/changelog spoofing** — a way to make `callisto version` compute or apply an incorrect bump, or inject arbitrary content into a generated changelog, that a maintainer could plausibly merge without noticing.
- **Git operation safety** — `callisto_model::vcs` runs the system `git` binary; argument injection through ref names or paths, or unsafe handling of an untrusted repository (submodules, refs, hooks), is in scope.

Dependency vulnerabilities are already checked continuously via `just audit` (`cargo deny check advisories`) in CI — a report that only restates an existing advisory `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` already flags isn't a new finding, but a way to bypass or disable that check is.

Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Cargo, npm, PyPI, or GitHub Actions themselves — report those to the respective platform.

## Supported Versions

Security fixes land on `main` and the latest published release of each affected crate. Given Callisto is pre-1.0, older minor versions are not backported — upgrade to the latest release.

# Architecture decision records

- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.
- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — proposed v1 correction; not accepted or implemented. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.

## Rules

- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.
- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.
